questions.title: The junction that barriers diffusion between cells
questions.question: Which of the following structures acts as a barrier to diffusion between adjacent cells?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The gap junction (nexus) leaves a narrow gap bridged by channel proteins that let ions and small molecules pass between cells — it is a communication route, not a diffusion barrier.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The desmosome (macula adherens) is an adhesion spot anchoring intermediate filaments between cells; it holds cells together mechanically but leaves the intercellular space open, so it does not seal against diffusion.
explanations.C: Correct. The tight (occluding) junction, the zonula occludens, is the most apical of the lateral junctions. Its adjacent plasma membranes actually fuse at points through transmembrane proteins, obliterating the intercellular space at those points and encircling the apex of the cell like a belt. This makes the epithelium a barrier rather than a sieve, forcing anything crossing it to pass through the cells rather than between them.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The hemidesmosome anchors a cell's basal surface to the underlying basement membrane, not to an adjacent cell, so it plays no role in sealing the space between neighbouring cells.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the tight junction (zonula occludens) as the epithelial diffusion barrier, distinct from the gap junction, desmosome and hemidesmosome.
